title: 2025 operating budget review and 3.9% tax increase
subtitle: Library and Centre in the Square budgets, $1M strategic fund, tax bill communication, enterprise budgets including parking
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held the first of its 2025 budget meetings, focused on the operating budget. Staff proposed a 3.9% city tax rate increase. With the water infrastructure program increase, staff estimated an impact of $131 on the average household. The city's share of the property tax bill is 30%, with the Region of Waterloo at 58% and school boards at 12%.

The committee heard from Kitchener Public Library and Centre in the Square about their 2025 budgets. Both boards received operating grant increases of 2.6%. The library grant includes funding for the new Southwest Library. Staff also presented the seven self-funded enterprises: building, golf, parking, water, sanitary, stormwater and gas.

Councillors discussed how to explain the tax bill split better, and the $1 million of unallocated one-time funding for a strategic priority. The committee received the operating budget report for information {{vote:m1}}. No budget decisions were made. The mayor is to table the budget on December 2, and final approval is scheduled for December 12, 2024. Staff will return on November 25 with a communication plan.

decisions.detail: The committee received the 2025 Operating Budget report (FIN-2024-495) for information, with final approval left to Final Budget Day on December 12, 2024.

debate: Several councillors said residents often blame the city for tax increases, though the city collects only 30% of the bill. They asked for stronger communication than the existing bill insert. One suggested changing the bank withdrawal label, but staff said it must show the City of Kitchener as collector.

Staff said the bill format is standard. They offered to bring back communication objectives on November 25 before discussing tactics. One councillor said seniors and people not online may miss social media messaging.

Councillors asked about Centre in the Square's budget presentation. Staff said it now shows gross revenues and expenses instead of net amounts, so totals look larger but the bottom line is unchanged. A delegate said this gives a fuller picture of the business.
Councillors asked Centre in the Square to improve food and beverage options and revenue beyond performances, and said they had asked for this for years. A delegate said improvements are planned.

On parking, a councillor asked whether the budget under-estimates revenue. Staff recommended waiting for a review of the parking enterprise, to be reported next year. Staff said the $1M one-time funding would return to reserves if unspent, not lower the tax increase.
